summaries: A U.S. Census Bureau and HUD statistical release on new residential construction for August 2022, published September 20, 2022. Relevant to the task, Table 3b provides monthly, not seasonally adjusted single-family housing starts ("1 unit") by region (Northeast, Midwest, South, West) for August 2022. This document covers the first month of the requested 2022/08–2025/05 timeframe. It lists South single-family starts as 46.1 thousand, compared to 5.4 thousand (Northeast), 11.6 thousand (Midwest), and 20.0 thousand (West). As an early release, the August 2022 figures are marked preliminary ('p') and may be subject to revision by later reports in the collection, which would prevail according to the task's precedence rule. No data is provided for September 2022 through May 2025.

A U.S. Census Bureau and HUD press release (October 19, 2022) on new residential construction for September 2022. Relevant to the task: Table 3b provides "Not seasonally adjusted" data for "New Privately-Owned Housing Units Started," specifically the "1 unit" (single-family) column broken down by region (Northeast, Midwest, South, West). The document supplies monthly figures for August 2022 (revised) and September 2022 (preliminary), covering the start of the requested 2022/08–2025/05 window. It enables the comparison of South single-family starts against other regions for these two months, though it does not contain data for the period from October 2022 onwards.

Relevant to the task, Table 3b provides "Not seasonally adjusted" monthly housing starts data for single-family units ("1 unit") broken down by region (Northeast, Midwest, South, West). The table covers monthly figures from January 2022 through October 2022, supplying the specific volume figures required to compare the South against other regions for the August, September, and October 2022 portion of the requested 2022/08 to 2025/05 timeframe. It lists the South's single-family starts for these months as 44.9, 43.6, and 42.1 thousand, respectively, allowing for regional comparison during this specific window, though it lacks coverage for the remainder of the requested timeframe. The August and September figures are marked as revised, while the October figure is preliminary.
